obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reporting
basis: No final rule. As proposed, 226.2(a) would not reach the shop (7 employees against the 800-employee SBA size standard for NAICS 335311, 13 CFR 121.201), but the sector criterion in proposed 226.2(b)(3) covers electrical equipment, appliance and component manufacturing regardless of size, so the shop would likely be covered if the rule is finalized as proposed

obligation: ICTS supply chain: connected vehicles rule
basis: Applies to connected vehicle manufacturers and VCS hardware importers. The shop repairs and remanufactures transformers and makes no vehicles or vehicle systems
The shop has never exported: all customers are in Florida and neighboring states and no shipment left the United States

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 (and NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC through it)
basis: No DoD contracts or subcontracts. The one federal order is from a civilian agency and has no DFARS clauses

obligation: NERC CIP-013-2 supply chain risk management (direct)
applies: No (reaches the shop only through the cooperative exhibit)
basis: CIP-013-2 applies to the Responsible Entities in its section 4.1, such as the G&T cooperative. The shop is a vendor, not a NERC-registered entity

obligation: G&T cooperative Vendor Cyber Security Exhibit
citation: Contract: master service agreement exhibit; flows down CIP-013-2 R1 Parts 1.2.1 to 1.2.3
basis: The shop works in the cooperative's substations and two staff hold cooperative badges. The exhibit requires incident notice within 72 hours of confirmation, response coordination, and access-revocation notice within 1 business day. These are contract terms, not NERC requirements

applies: No (not yet effective; binds the cooperative)
basis: Effective 2028-07-01. The cooperative may revise its exhibit before then

obligation: Basic safeguarding of covered contractor information systems
basis: The federal purchase order incorporates the clause, and FCI (agency drawings, unit records, delivery schedule, test reports for the agency units) resides in the shop's email, shared drive, ERP and test PC. No subcontracts are placed under the order, so the flow-down in (c) has nothing to apply to

obligation: Prohibition on covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment
basis: Incorporated in the order and prescribed in all contracts. Paragraph (b)(2) applies to equipment the shop uses whether or not the use is in performance of the order; report within 1 business day of identification under (d)

obligation: Prohibition on Kaspersky Lab covered articles
basis: Incorporated in the order and prescribed in all contracts; report within 3 business days of identification

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (reasonable measures and breach notification)
basis: The shop holds personal information of 7 current and about 15 former employees in its HR and payroll files

obligation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3
basis: No binding sector-wide cyber rule applies to critical manufacturing; CSF 2.0 with the OT guide is the benchmark for the gap analysis

obligation: Customer purchase order and confidentiality terms
basis: Customer orders call for a test report with each unit and set delivery terms; the cooperative's master service agreement treats substation locations and equipment data as confidential information
Notice as soon as practicable through the 24x7 breach hotline; panel counsel and forensics

obligation: OFAC sanctions risk for ransomware payments
citation: OFAC advisory of 2021-09-21; 31 CFR ch. V
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons before any ransom payment

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: Customers pay by bank transfer or check; no payment card data is handled

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The shop is not a health care provider, health plan or clearinghouse and holds no health information for others
